fail_closed_rules: Energy National Policy Statements guide NSIP decision-making but do not grant planning permission to a parcel or establish a project-specific route.
The EN-1 national need case is strategic and must not be converted into parcel-level need, value uplift or development probability.
EN-3 renewable-energy policy supports assessment of relevant NSIPs but does not make a solar, wind or storage proposal acceptable by default.
EN-5 electricity-network policy does not identify an exact legal corridor, easement, substation boundary or connection point for a parcel.
Pre-application consultation, acceptance or examination of an NSIP application is not a Development Consent Order grant.
A granted DCO does not by itself prove every land right, connection agreement, discharge of requirement, construction milestone or commercial operation date.
Electricity Act section 37 consent for an electric line is a distinct consent route and must not be treated as generic planning permission for associated development.
National Grid transmission route maps are approximate and indicative; they are not legal title, easement or survey-grade parcel boundaries.
A mapped transmission substation location is approximate infrastructure context and does not establish the legal operational compound or safeguarding envelope.
Electricity transmission and electricity distribution networks have different operators, voltage roles, datasets and connection processes and must not be collapsed into one layer.
An overhead-line centreline or cable route does not establish ownership, wayleave, easement width, safety clearance or developable setback without authoritative project evidence.
The existence of a nearby substation does not prove spare capacity, feasible connection, connection cost or an available bay.
A National Grid siting study or options process does not prove that an emerging substation site has been selected, consented or acquired.
Gate 2 status is a connection-queue status and does not equal planning permission, land ownership, financing or construction readiness in every other regime.
Gate 1 status is not a planning refusal and does not prove that a project will never connect or cannot progress through a later gated process.
A TEC contract/register entry is not evidence that a project is built, energised, operational or producing the registered capacity.
TEC register capacity may contain aggregate or duplicate presentations across stages and technologies; raw totals must not be treated as unique installed capacity.
A connection offer or contractual connection date is not a guarantee of network reinforcement completion, energisation or project commercial operation by that date.
Published Gate 2 to Whole Queue batch windows describe programme sequencing and must not be turned into an exact individual project offer date without project evidence.
Connections reform criteria, timetables and queue outcomes are time-sensitive and must be verified against the current NESO and Ofgem position before use.
Strategic alignment under connections reform is not planning approval and does not resolve environmental, land, consenting or local-planning constraints.
A readiness declaration is evidence for the connections process and must not be treated as conclusive legal-title, planning-consent or construction evidence outside that process.
Future Energy Scenarios are pathways, not forecasts or commitments, and must not be downscaled into parcel-level demand or generation predictions.
ETYS identifies system requirements and constraints at network scale; it is not a project approval, final route or parcel-specific capacity statement.
A CSNP recommendation or strategic-network option is not a DCO, planning permission, compulsory acquisition power or final detailed route.
Regional or strategic energy planning outputs do not themselves create a distribution or transmission connection offer for a parcel.
RIIO-T3 allowances, incentives and reporting frameworks regulate network companies and do not prove that a named reinforcement is consented, funded to completion or operational.
Battery capacity reported in a connections queue is not installed or operating battery capacity and must not be combined with operational generation totals.
REPD status is a dated project-monitoring record and must be checked for current planning, construction and operational status before parcel-level use.
An REPD project marked operational does not establish current output, availability, ownership or exact as-built boundary for parcel analysis.
Planning Data infrastructure-project-type is a taxonomy/reference dataset and does not itself provide authoritative project geometry or consent status.
Planning Data work on National Grid substation sites is screen-stage and licence-restricted/indicative; absence or approximate records must not be interpreted as no substation constraint.
Renewable and low-carbon planning guidance lists considerations but does not predetermine the outcome of an individual planning application.
Fire and rescue engagement for qualifying battery energy storage proposals is a planning-safety consideration and not an approval or refusal decision.
Generation-capacity thresholds determine consenting routes only in context; they must not be used as a generic approval threshold or parcel suitability score.
A DCO decision for one solar or wind project is project-specific precedent/evidence and must not be generalized into consent for a different site.
Overhead lines, underground cables, substations, generating stations and battery storage are distinct asset and consent classes and must remain separately typed.
National Grid consultation and interactive project maps can show emerging options that may change; consultation geometry is not a final consented route.
Community-benefit funding associated with hosting network infrastructure is not planning permission, compensation entitlement, land acquisition or proof the project will proceed.
